farraa:1-1.t:
His saying, Blessed and Exalted is He: ﴿يٰأَيُّهَا ٱلْمُدَّثِّرُ﴾.
He means: the one who has covered himself with his garments in order to sleep.

farraa:11-11.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ذَرْنِي وَمَنْ خَلَقْتُ وَحِيداً﴾.
There are two ways in [الوحيد]. Some said: leave Me [alone] with him whom I created by Myself alone. Others said: I created him alone, having neither wealth nor sons; and this is the more comprehensive of the two ways.

farraa:12-12.t:
His saying, Blessed and Exalted is He: ﴿وَجَعَلْتُ لَهُ مَالاً مَّمْدُوداً﴾.
Al-Kalbī said: goods, gold and silver. [Abū al-ʿAbbās told us, he said:] Muḥammad told us, he said: al-Farrāʾ told us, he said: and Qays told me, from Ibrāhīm ibn al-Muhājir, from Mujāhid, concerning His saying: ﴿وَجَعَلْتُ لَهُ مَالاً مَّمْدُوداً﴾; he said: a thousand dinars. We think that "extended" (mamdūd) was used for the number because a thousand is the limit of number: from a thousand one goes back to the beginning of counting. Similar to it is the Arabs' saying: لك على ألف أقدع (I owe you a full thousand), i.e. the limit of number.

farraa:13-13.t:
His saying: ﴿وَبَنِينَ شُهُوداً﴾.
He had ten sons who were never absent from his sight, either for trade or for work. And "the one alone" is al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra al-Makhzūmī.

farraa:18-18.t:
His saying: ﴿إِنَّهُ فَكَّرَ وَقَدَّرَ﴾.
They mention that he gathered the chiefs of the people of Mecca and said: The season [of pilgrimage] has drawn near, and the affair of this man has spread among the people; what will you say about him to the people? They said: We will say: [he is] mad. He said: Then people will come to him and speak with him, and he will be seen to be sane and sound, and they will call you liars. They said: We will say: a poet. He said: They are Arabs who have transmitted poems and know them, and Muḥammad's speech does not resemble poetry. They said: We will say: a soothsayer. He said: They know the soothsayers [112/b] and have questioned them, and they do not say: such and such will happen, if Allah wills; whereas Muḥammad tells you nothing without saying: if Allah wills. Then he stood up, and they said: al-Walīd has turned Sabian (ṣabaʾa) — meaning: al-Walīd has become Muslim. His nephew Abū Jahl said: I will deal with him for you. He went to him and said: Quraysh claim that you have turned Sabian, and they want to collect for you wealth that will suffice you in place of what you want to eat of the leftovers of Muḥammad's ﷺ companions. He said: Woe to you! By Allah, they never have their fill, so how would I seek their leftovers when I am the wealthiest of Quraysh? But I have been thinking about the affair of Muḥammad ﷺ, and what we should answer the Arabs when they ask us; and I have resolved to say: a sorcerer. This is the interpretation of His saying: ﴿إِنَّهُ فَكَّرَ وَقَدَّرَ﴾: [he reflected and determined] what to say about Muḥammad ﷺ.

farraa:19-19.t:
His saying: ﴿فَقُتِلَ كَيْفَ قَدَّرَ﴾.
قُتل, that is: he was cursed. Likewise ﴿قاتلهم الله﴾ and ﴿قُتِلَ الإِنْسَانُ ما أَكْفَرَهُ﴾: it is mentioned that these [mean] cursing.

farraa:2-2.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قُمْ فَأَنذِرْ﴾.
He means: arise and pray, and command [others] to pray.

farraa:21-22.t:
His saying: ﴿ثُمَّ نَظَرَ ثُمَّ عَبَسَ وَبَسَرَ﴾.
They mention that he passed by a group of Muslims in the Sacred Mosque, and they said: Will you come to Islam, O Abū al-Mughīra? He said: Your companion is nothing but a sorcerer, and his speech is nothing but sorcery that he learned from Musaylima the Liar and from the sorcerers of Babylon. Then — He said — he turned away from them in arrogance, having frowned and scowled: he grimaced, too proud to believe.

farraa:24-24.t: That is His saying: ﴿إِنْ هَذَآ إِلاَّ سِحْرٌ يُؤْثَرُ﴾: he transmits it from the people of Babylon.

farraa:26-26.t:
Allah, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿سَأُصْلِيهِ سَقَرَ﴾.
It is one of the names of Hell; for that reason it is not made fully declinable (lam yujra), and likewise "لظى".

farraa:29-29.t:
His saying: ﴿لَوَّاحَةٌ لِّلْبَشَرِ﴾.
It is joined back to سقر with the intention of repetition, as He said: ﴿ذُو الْعَرْشِ الْمَجِيدُ فَعَّالٌ لِمَا يُرِيدُ﴾, and as He said in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: ﴿وَهَذَا بَعْلِى شَيْخاً﴾. Had it been "لواحةً للبشر" [in the accusative], it would be correct,
as He said: ﴿إِنَّهَا لإِحْدَى ٱلْكُبَرِ(35) نَذِيراً لِّلْبَشَرِ﴾ (36). In the reading of Ubayy: "نذِيرٌ لِلْبشَر"; and all are correct.
[Translator's note: «وَهَذَا بَعْلِى شَيْخاً» is as printed; this is the standard reading, and the reading of ʿAbd Allāh usually cited at this point is «شيخٌ».]
His saying: ﴿لَوَّاحَةٌ لِِّلْبَشَرِ﴾.
It blackens the skin (البَشَر) by burning it.

farraa:30-31.t:
His saying: ﴿عَلَيْهَا تِسْعَةَ عَشَرَ﴾.
The Arabs give fatḥa to [the numbers] from أحد عشر to تسعة عشر in the genitive and the nominative [alike]. Some of them lighten the ʿayn in تسعة عشر, giving the ʿayn sukūn in the masculine; but they do not lighten it in ثلاث عشرة to تسع عشرة, because they only lightened [it] in the masculine because of the large number of vowels. As for the feminine, the shīn of عشْرة has sukūn, so they did not lighten its ʿayn, lest two quiescent letters meet. Likewise اثنا عشر in the masculine: the ʿayn is not lightened, because the alif of اثنا عشر is quiescent, so another letter is not given sukūn after it, lest two quiescent letters meet.
[Translator's note: «خفضوا» ("put in the genitive") is as printed; in context it means «خففوا» ("lightened").]
One of the unbelievers of the people of Mecca, namely Abū Jahl, said: And what are nineteen? A man among us can overpower one and keep him off the people. And a man of Banū Jumaḥ, whose kunya was Abū al-Ashaddayn, said: I will take care of seventeen for you; you take care of two for me. So Allah sent down: ﴿وَمَا جَعَلْنَآ أَصْحَابَ ٱلنَّارِ إِلاَّ مَلاَئِكَةً﴾, i.e.: and who can overpower the angels? Then He said: ﴿وَمَا جَعَلْنَا عِدَّتَهُمْ ﴾ in its smallness ﴿إِلاَّ فِتْنَةً﴾ for those who disbelieve, so that they would say what they said. Then He said: ﴿لِيَسْتَيْقِنَ ٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُواْ ٱلْكِتَابَ﴾: certainty added to their certainty, because the number of the keepers of Hell in their Book is nineteen; ﴿وَيَزْدَادَ ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُوۤاْ إِيمَاناً﴾ because it is likewise in the Book of the People of the Book.

farraa:33-33.t:
His saying: ﴿وَٱللَّيْلِ إِذْ أَدْبَرَ﴾.
Ibn ʿAbbās read it: "والليل إذَا دَبر", and Mujāhid and some of the people of Medina likewise; and many people read it: "واللَّيْل إذْ أَدْبَر". [Abū al-ʿAbbās told us, he said: Muḥammad told us, he said:] al-Farrāʾ told us, he said: Muḥammad ibn al-Faḍl told me that, from ʿAṭāʾ, from Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from Zayd, that he read it: "والليل إذْ أَدْبَر". In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh it is: "والليل إذا أدبر", and al-Ḥasan read it likewise: "إذا أدبر", as ʿAbd Allāh did.
[Abū al-ʿAbbās told us, he said: Muḥammad told us,] he said: al-Farrāʾ told us, he said: and Qays told me, from ʿAlī ibn al-Aqmar, from a man — I know him only as al-Agharr — from Ibn ʿAbbās, that he read: "والليل إذا دَبَر".
And he said: أدبر is only [said of] the back of a camel [i.e. being galled]. [Abū al-ʿAbbās told us, he said: Muḥammad told us,] he said: al-Farrāʾ told us, he said: and Qays told us, from ʿAlī ibn al-Aqmar, from Abū ʿAṭiyya, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, that he read "أدبر". [Al-Farrāʾ said: I think Abū ʿAṭiyya can only be al-Wādiʿī — indeed it is he. And al-Farrāʾ said: there is no إذ in Qays's report, and I consider the two only as two dialect forms.] One says: دبر النساء (sic), and the winter and the summer أدبر (went away); and likewise قَبَل and أقبل. But when they say: أقبل الراكب وأدبر (the rider came and went), they say it only with alif. To me the two are one in meaning; I do not rule out that what occurs with time-periods may occur with men.
[Translator's note: «دبر النساء» is as printed; «الشتاء» ("winter") or similar appears to be intended.]

farraa:35-35.t:
His saying: ﴿إِنَّهَا لإِحْدَى ٱلْكُبَرِ﴾.
The هاء is a pronoun standing for Hell.

farraa:36-36.t:
His saying: ﴿نَذِيراً لِّلْبَشَرِ﴾.
One of the grammarians used to say: "نذيراً" is accusative [by] the beginning of the sura: O Muḥammad, arise as a warner to mankind. That is nothing, and Allah knows best, because much speech has come in between them, and its nominative in the reading of Ubayy rules out this meaning. Its accusative [rather] comes from His saying: ﴿إِنَّها لإحدى الكُبر نذيراً﴾: you detach it (taqṭaʿuhu) from the definite, because "إحدى الكبر" is definite, so you detached it from it [making it a ḥāl (circumstantial)]. Its accusative may also be by making النذير mean "warning", from His saying: ﴿لاَ تُبْقِى وَلاَ تَذَرُ﴾ لواحة [— you tell this about Hell as a warning] to mankind; for نذير may have the meaning of إنذار (warning). Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said: ﴿كَيْفَ نَذِير﴾ and ﴿فَكَيْفَ كان نكِير﴾, meaning: My warning and My reproach.

farraa:39-42.t:
His saying: ﴿إِلاَّ أَصْحَابَ ٱلْيَمِينِ﴾.
Al-Kalbī said: they are the people of Paradise. [Abū al-ʿAbbās told us, he said:] al-Farrāʾ told us, he said: and al-Fuḍayl ibn ʿIyāḍ told me, from Manṣūr ibn al-Muʿtamir, from al-Minhāl, tracing it back to ʿAlī, who said: ﴿إِلاَّ أَصْحَابَ ٱلْيَمِينِ﴾ — he said: they are the children. This seems right, because the children have not earned anything for which they would be held in pledge; and in His saying: ﴿يَتَسَآءَلُونَ عَنِ ٱلْمُجْرِمِينَ مَا سَلَكَكُمْ فِي سَقَرَ﴾ there is what strengthens [the view] that they are the children, because they did not know sins, so they asked: ﴿مَا سَلَكَكُمْ فِي سَقَرَ﴾.

farraa:4-4.t:
His saying, Blessed and Exalted is He: ﴿وَثِيَابَكَ فَطَهِّرْ﴾.
He is saying: do not be treacherous and so defile your garments, for the treacherous man is "soiled of garments". It is also said: "and purify your garments" [means] and set right your deeds. Some said: "and purify your garments" means: shorten them, for shortening garments is purification.

farraa:5-5.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَٱلرُّجْزَ فَٱهْجُرْ﴾.
ʿĀṣim, al-Aʿmash and al-Ḥasan read it with kasra [الرِّجز], and al-Sulamī, Mujāhid and the people of Medina read it with ḍamma, reading: "والرجزُ فاهجر". Mujāhid explained: الرجز means the idols; and al-Kalbī explained it: الرجز is the punishment. We think that they are two dialect forms and that the meaning in both [112/a] is one.
[Translator's note: the source writes «والرجزُ» with a ḍamma on the zāy, while the point under discussion is the vowel of the rāʾ (الرُّجز).]

farraa:50-50.t:
His saying: ﴿كَأَنَّهُمْ حُمُرٌ مُّسْتَنْفِرَةٌ﴾.
ʿĀṣim and al-Aʿmash read it: "مستنفِرة" with kasra, and the people of the Ḥijāz read it: "مستنفَرة" with fatḥa on the fāʾ; both are frequent in the speech of the Arabs. The poet said:
أمْسِكْ حِمارَكَ إِنَّهُ مُسْتنفِرٌ * فى إِثرِ أحْمِرَةٍ عَمْدنَ لِغُرّبِ
(Hold back your donkey, for it is bolting after she-asses that have made for Ghurrab.)
As for القسورة, it is said that it is the archers; and al-Kalbī said, with his chain of transmission: it is the lion.
[Abū al-ʿAbbās told us, he said: Muḥammad told us, he said:] al-Farrāʾ told us, he said: Abū al-Aḥwaṣ told me, from Saʿīd ibn Masrūq, [father of] Abū Sufyān al-Thawrī, from ʿIkrima, who said: It was said to him: القسورة is the lion in the language of the Abyssinians. He said: القسورة are the archers; the lion in the language of the Abyssinians is ʿanbasa.

farraa:52-52.t:
His saying: ﴿بَلْ يُرِيدُ كُلُّ ٱمْرِىءٍ مِّنْهُمْ أَن يُؤْتَىٰ صُحُفاً مُّنَشَّرَةً﴾.
The unbelievers of Quraysh said to the Prophet ﷺ [114/a]: When a man among the Children of Israel committed a sin, his sin would be found written on a sheet in the morning; so why do we not see that? So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿بَلْ يُرِيدُ كُلُّ ٱمْرِىءٍ مِّنْهُمْ أَن يُؤْتَىٰ صُحُفاً مُّنَشَّرَةً﴾.

farraa:54-54.t:
His saying: ﴿إِنَّهُ تَذْكِرَةٌ﴾.
He means this Qurʾān. Had it been said: "إنها تذكرةٌ", it would be correct, as He said in [Sūrat] ʿAbasa. Whoever says (إنها) means the sura, and whoever says (إنه) means the Qurʾān.

farraa:6-6.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلاَ تَمْنُن تَسْتَكْثِرُ﴾.
He is saying: do not give anything in this world in order to receive more than it. In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: "ولا تَمْنُن أنْ تَسْتَكْثِرَ", and this is evidence for the indicative (rafʿ) in "تستكثر". Had it been made jussive with this meaning, it would be correct; but the indicative is the way of the reading and of practice.

farraa:8-8.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَإِذَا نُقِرَ فِي ٱلنَّاقُورِ﴾.
It is said that it is the first of the two blasts.
